cases.title: Grounded scan summary

notes: Clean fixtures are useful to confirm MESA does not invent findings in a simple baseline.
limitations: This system is synthetic and smaller than a real service repository.

notes: Chatty services are still inferred from static call-site count, not real runtime traffic.

This fixture behaves like a concentrated hotspot and is useful for roadmap, health, and priority evaluation together.
limitations: It is still a synthetic benchmark even though it combines multiple anti-pattern signals.

notes: This benchmark is a useful stand-in for distributed monolith symptoms, but it is not a real production repository.

Unlike the other seeded fixtures (mostly one anti-pattern per system), this system deliberately interleaves five anti-patterns across 8 services in one scan: a 3-node CYCLIC_DEPENDENCY (checkout-service -> billing-gateway-service -> fulfillment-service -> checkout-service), a CHATTY_SERVICE pair (alert-service -> profile-service, 4 static call sites), a 3-service SHARED_DATABASE (checkout-service, billing-gateway-service, ledger-service all reference platform_ledger_db), a GOD_SERVICE hotspot (platform-hub-service, scoring exactly at the 70.0 HIGH-risk threshold with 10 endpoints and 7 distinct outbound targets), and source-level HARD_CODED_SERVICE_DEPENDENCY findings including 2 private-IP references in legacy-bridge-service.

The 3 services sharing platform_ledger_db (checkout-service, billing-gateway-service, ledger-service) each also produce a HARD_CODED_SERVICE_DEPENDENCY finding purely from the literal `db-host:5432` substring inside their database connection string: this is the existing generic host:port hard-coded-endpoint pattern matching independently of the separate database-connection extraction that produces the SHARED_DATABASE finding. Not a bug specific to this fixture - the same DB connection string is legitimately both a database reference and a literal host:port pattern - but worth noting since it means 'one line' can produce two different finding types.

This benchmark exists specifically to test recall (does MESA find everything that is really there) on a single system with multiple overlapping anti-patterns, complementing the real-repository benchmarks in benchmarks/real_repo_*.yml, which mostly tested precision on comparatively clean architectures. See docs/research/THREATS_TO_VALIDITY.md.
limitations: This is still a synthetic, hand-authored fixture, not a real repository; it demonstrates MESA can find multiple co-occurring anti-patterns in one scan, not that real messy systems look exactly like this.
